_meta.note: Louisiana legislative election-date correction. 144 LA state legislators advertised a next election of 2026-11-03. Louisiana holds no 2026 legislative election - four-year terms, last elected Oct/Nov 2023, next Oct/Nov 2027 - so every one of these pages told a voter their legislator was on the November 3 ballot. This defect PRE-DATES tonight's work: verified against a pre-change snapshot of scorecard.json, where all 144 already carried 2026-11-03; enrich-elections.py has no LA rule and did not write them. The date is cleared, not replaced (blank beats wrong). Each record's existing profile.confidence is passed through explicitly so the engine does not stamp evidence_<tier>. No rubric cell is touched.

bob-owen@LA.notes_append: Election-currency correction 2026-10-03: this record carried next_election_date 2026-11-03, but Louisiana holds NO state legislative election in 2026. Both chambers serve four-year terms and were last elected October 14 / November 18, 2023; sources place the next legislative election on October 16 / November 20, 2027. Louisiana is one of four states (with Mississippi, New Jersey and Virginia) with zero legislative seats on the 2026 ballot. The false 2026 date is CLEARED rather than replaced: per scorecard doctrine blank beats wrong, and the 2027 date is not yet confirmed against a Louisiana Secretary of State calendar. With no date, build_election_html renders no 'Next Election' banner, so the page no longer tells a Louisiana voter their legislator is on the ballot in 31 days.
